newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti sells PCs to Piedmont - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti sells PCs to Piedmont - CEO.

text.p: Italian information technology company Olivetti is selling its personal computer division to a new company, Piedmont, in which Olivetti will have a 10 percent stake, Chief Executive Officer Roberto Colaninno said Monday.

Colaninno told a joint news conference in Milan with U.S. financier Edward Gottesman the PC division was being sold for 250 billion to 300 billion lire ($159 million to $190 million) to the new company.
Gottesman said information on ownership of Piedmont International would be announced in due course.
Gottesman and Colaninno told the news conference that Gianmario Rossignolo, chairman of AB Electrolux unit Zanussi, had agreed to become executive chairman of Piedmont.
As part of the deal, the Olivetti brand will be licensed to Piedmont for four years.
Colaninno said after two years Olivetti had the option to sell its 10 percent stake to Piedmont, which Piedmont had to buy.
"A formula has been decided to determine the price," he said.

Olivetti has been seeking a buyer since late last year for the PC division, which, under former chairman Carlo De Benedetti, made the company's name in the 1980s but which has since suffered losses in the competitive climate of the 1990s.
